newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower, gilt prices rally.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower, gilt prices rally.

text.p: Indian call money ended 0.25-1.50 percent on Monday, down from the day's opening level of 1.25-2.00 percent, dealers said.
There were some stray deals at 2.50 percent, they said.
The next fortnight may see call rates raising, as advance tax outflows of approximately 50 billion rupees will be withdrawn from the system before December 17, dealers said

"RBI announcement on cash reserve ratio (CRR) cut by 0.5 percent in January is unlikely to have any impact on the market as the RBI will take out the liquidity in the form of open market operation and repo transactions, which will put pressure on call rate," said a dealer.
"It looks RBI want's to stabilise the call rates to 5.0 percent levels," he said referring to RBI governor's statement in Beijing about a fresh CRR cut in January.
The government securities market was active, with lot of action in the newly-auctioned 13.55 percent stock maturing in 2001, dealers said.
"The securities market was comparatively active, as call eased," said Mithi Somesh at Lloyds Brokerage Ltd.
"Activities shifted from the short-dated securities of 1997 and 1998 maturities to 2000 and 2001 maturity papers," he said.
Somesh said Monday's trading volume on the National Stock Exchange was 1.94 billion rupees, up from Saturday's 1.74 billion rupees.
The price of 13.55 percent 2001 stock rose by 10 basis points to 100.19 rupees in the speculative trading, with a volume of 400 million rupees, he said.
The 13.50 percent 1997 stock rose by five basis points to 102.80 rupees compared Saturday's close of 102.75 rupees.
Similarly, the zero coupon bonds maturing in 1999 and 2000 rose by five basis points each to 76.78 rupees and 62.50 rupees respectively, dealers said.

Treasury bills were steady, most of the activity confined to the 364 day papers. Commercial paper for Thermax maturing in January was traded at 10.10 percent, while Wockhardt's paper maturing in February was traded at 11.25 percent, dealers said.
